title: Payment service and policies
idea: The core design is one PaymentService facade that dedupes by Idempotency-Key, sends each method to a PaymentGateway, and asks a RetryPolicy whether to try again.

analogy.text: A cashier at a busy counter. One cashier takes every payment, hands cards to the card machine and UPI to the QR scanner, and follows the store's retry rule.
analogy.breaks: A cashier remembers faces; the service remembers only keys.

points: `PaymentService` is a facade: callers see one `pay` method.
Each `PaymentGateway` says which methods it supports; the service picks one.
`RetryPolicy` is the strategy pattern: retry timeouts, never declines.
A repeated Idempotency-Key returns the stored Payment without calling a gateway.

hero.title: One card payment through the service

steps.caption: Order ORD-2 pays 15000 by card with key `k-2`.
PaymentService checks its key map first. `k-2` is new, so it creates P-2.
CardGateway supports CardPayment, so it gets the charge. Attempt 1 times out.
RetryPolicy allows another try: the result was a timeout and attempts are under the limit.
Attempt 2 sends the same payment id, so the gateway can dedupe it. It is approved.
P-2 returns SUCCEEDED with two attempts recorded.
The client retries `k-2` after a dropped response. The service finds P-2 in its map.
The stored P-2 comes back at once. No gateway is called again.

code.title: Service and interfaces
code.caption: The core flow. Gateways and the retry rule are interfaces passed into the constructor. The map is not thread-safe yet; page 5 fixes that.

walk.text: Wire two gateways and a fixed retry policy of three attempts.
A UPI payment and its replay, a flaky card and its replay, a declined card.
Two interfaces are the swap points: gateways and the retry rule.
The fake card gateway times out on its first call and declines one token.
FixedRetry retries only TIMEOUT, and only below the attempt limit.
A known key returns the stored Payment. The key is claimed only after a gateway is found.
Charge until the policy says stop. A final timeout leaves PROCESSING, not FAILED.

code.title: A new retry policy
code.caption: Exponential backoff added as a new RetryPolicy class. The loop in main mirrors `PaymentService.pay`; passing the new policy to its constructor is the only change.

walk.text: The policy gets a Sleeper that records waits instead of sleeping, so the run is fast and repeatable.
Replay a scripted gateway: three timeouts, then an approval.
Ask whether a decline would be retried.
A new class: each retry waits twice as long as the one before.

pitfalls: Retry a timed-out charge with the same payment id, or the gateway may charge twice.
Never retry a DECLINED result; the bank has already answered.
Do not branch on method type inside the service; add a gateway class.

quiz.q: What does CorePayment print for key k-3?
quiz.why: `tok_declined` returns DECLINED. FixedRetry retries only TIMEOUT, so one attempt ends in FAILED. The k-1 replay created no payment, so the id is P-3.

takeaway: One facade, one gateway per method, and retry rules behind an interface.
